Well, I'm 55 now, been working this land for 30 years since I got my ag degree. Only 4.1 mu, but I know every corner of it. My son's family works off-farm in Handan, so it's mainly me and my wife in the field, though they come back for harvest. Money's tight — 4.1 mu won't make you rich — but I understand soil and plant nutrition, so I don't waste inputs.

This year I'm planting Jimai 26 wheat on all 4.1 mu in mid-October. I'm targeting 450 kg/mu, which means I need about 19 kg N/mu total — 7.5 kg from 50 kg of 15-15-15 compound as base, then 11.5 kg from urea at jointing in late March. I'll also get 7.5 kg P and 7.5 kg K from the base. Four irrigations: winter water in late November, green-up in late March, jointing in April, and one at grain filling in May. Each irrigation costs electricity, so I stop at four — I know the return on the fifth is poor. For weeds I'll spray herbicide, and I'll watch for disease at heading — if it's humid, I'll hit it with fungicide.

Come early June, the combine takes the wheat and I have maybe five days to get the maize in. I'm planting Zhengdan 958 hybrid — costs more for seed but the yield is worth it. Targeting 500 kg/mu. I'll put down 45 kg of compound fertilizer at planting and topdress with urea at big trumpet stage, total about 15 kg N/mu. Two irrigations: one after planting if the soil's dry, and a critical one at tasseling in early August. A post-emergence herbicide and insecticide for corn borer.

Total budget is about 3,400 yuan for both crops. That's most of my liquid cash, but my son sends some money from the city. I could cut fertilizer to save cash, but with university training I know that losing 50 kg yield costs more than the fertilizer. Still, I can't afford to over-apply either — every yuan matters on 4.1 mu.
